description: Two quick Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks: a narrow but real score suite, small enough to run repeatedly on one machine, floored for its own size. Never comparable to coder-effectiveness-v1 — different suite key.

$comment: Floors restored from the retired packages/coder-effectiveness/
thresholds/tb2-quick.json. minGradedTrials is 2, the whole suite: a
quick suite that graded one of its two tasks is a success rate over a
denominator of one. minSuccessRate 0.5 says at least one task must be
solved - the regression floor, not a target. maxUngradedRatio is 0
because with two trials the smallest non-zero ratio is a half. No
maxCostPerAcceptedOutcomeUsd: the lanes this suite runs on are either
unmetered (local Ollama) or unpriced in bench/rates.json, so a dollar
ceiling would leave the gate unverifiable on every run - a gate nobody
reads. Declare one in the same change that makes the lane priceable.

tasks.rationale: near-zero tool surface: the suite's test of whether the agent can just answer
a fully specified checklist: every command is known upfront, so round count is a tool habit rather than a reasoning result
